name: Tengyu Ma
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
research_topics: Automatic verification of natural-language mathematical proofs
Scaling laws for language model pretraining
Deep learning theory and nonconvex optimization
current_direction: Scaling LLM self-play for formal theorem proving in Lean4
Making natural-language proofs machine-verifiable (Pseudo-Formalization + Block Verification)
RL post-training to cut reasoning latency via parallel chain-of-thought
Empirical science of pretraining: honest optimizer benchmarking and configuration-aware scaling laws
Shift from pure DL theory toward large-scale empirical LLM/reasoning research
current_direction_basis: Driven by the five 2025-2026 papers verified on arXiv abstract pages and listed at the top of the faculty homepage's 'Selected or Recent Work' section, whose first topic block is now titled 'Reasoning Models & RL'. Self-play/theorem-proving direction from 'STP: Self-play LLM Theorem Provers' (2025, arXiv:2502.00212) and 'Scaling Self-Play with Self-Guidance' (2026, arXiv:2604.20209, Lean4, 200 rounds of self-play). Proof-verification direction from 'Pseudo-Formalization for Automatic Proof Verification' (2026, arXiv:2605.20531). Reasoning-latency/RL direction from 'Divide-and-Conquer CoT: RL for Reducing Latency via Parallel Reasoning' (2026, arXiv:2601.23027). Empirical-pretraining direction from 'Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them' (arXiv:2509.02046) and 'Configuration-to-Performance Scaling Law with Neural Ansatz' (2026, arXiv:2602.10300). The older self-description on the homepage ('nonconvex optimization, high-dimensional statistics') was NOT used to infer current direction.

evidence.title: Pseudo-Formalization for Automatic Proof Verification
evidence.summary: Proposes Pseudo-Formalization (PF), a proof format keeping the modularity/precision of formal proofs with the flexibility of natural language; an LLM translates a proof to PF then verifies each module independently ('Block Verification'). Pareto-dominates LLM-as-judge baselines on error-finding precision and recall; releases the ArxivMathGradingBench research-level proof verification benchmark. Authors: Slim Barkallah, Luke Bailey, Kaiyue Wen, Mohammed Abouzaid, Tengyu Ma. Submitted 19 May 2026, revised 17 Jun 2026.

evidence.title: Scaling Self-Play with Self-Guidance
evidence.summary: Introduces Self-Guided Self-Play (SGS), where the model acts as Solver, Conjecturer and a Guide that scores synthetic problems to prevent Conjecturer reward-hacking/collapse over long training runs. Applied to formal theorem proving in Lean4; a 7B model after 200 rounds of self-play solves more problems than a 671B model at pass@4. Authors: Luke Bailey, Kaiyue Wen, Kefan Dong, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Tengyu Ma. Submitted 22 Apr 2026, revised 11 Aug 2026.

evidence.title: Divide-and-Conquer CoT: RL for Reducing Latency via Parallel Reasoning
evidence.summary: Trains a model to act as a director that identifies parallelizable subtasks in its reasoning and spawns workers, using SFT plus a multi-stage RL algorithm with data filtering. On AIME 2024 and HMMT 2025 it matches DeepScaleR-1.5B-Preview accuracy while cutting longest-path length (a latency proxy) by 35-40%. Authors: Arvind Mahankali, Kaiyue Wen, Tengyu Ma. Submitted 30 Jan 2026.

evidence.title: Configuration-to-Performance Scaling Law with Neural Ansatz
evidence.summary: Learns a mapping from the full training configuration to pretraining performance, parameterized by an LLM and fit on diverse open-source pretraining logs (NCPL). Achieves 20-40% lower prediction error than the configuration-agnostic Chinchilla law and generalizes to runs using up to 10x more compute than any run in its training set. Authors: Huaqing Zhang, Kaiyue Wen, Tengyu Ma. Submitted 10 Feb 2026.

evidence.title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them
evidence.summary: Systematic study of ten deep learning optimizers across four model scales (0.1B-1.2B) and data-to-model ratios, arguing that unequal hyperparameter tuning and misleading evaluation setups have inflated claimed speedups. Finds matrix-preconditioner optimizers (Muon, Soap) fastest, but speedup over well-tuned AdamW shrinks from 1.4x at 0.1B to 1.1x at 1.2B. Authors: Kaiyue Wen, David Hall, Tengyu Ma, Percy Liang. Posted to arXiv 2 Sep 2025 (rev 4 Sep 2025); the faculty homepage lists this entry under year 2026, presumably for its conference venue.
